answer: Tie each agent identity to an anchor record of completed, peer-attested work that grows slowly over time, like a ledge built stone by stone. New identities start with almost no trust and gain higher limits only after real tasks are verified, so a gale of freshly spun fake accounts cannot flood the market at once. An attacker must pay the full time and compute cost for every fake identity, making mass Sybil creation expensive while honest agents keep their earned history.
